pages.hook: A live concert in the USA starts long before the first song. You show a ticket, find your section and your row, and wait with a loud, happy crowd.
pages.polite: If you need to pass people in your row, say **Excuse me** and **Thank you**. Do not stand in front of the people behind you.

mythfact.s: Many concert tickets in the USA are now on your phone.
mythfact.why: Mobile tickets are very common. You show a code at the door.

mythfact.s: An encore is the first song of the show.
mythfact.why: An encore is an extra song after the main show, when the crowd asks for more.

mythfact.s: Your ticket often tells you a section, a row and a seat.
mythfact.why: That is how you find your place: Section B, row five.

mythfact.s: Nobody sings with the band at a concert.
mythfact.why: Fans often sing along, and singers ask them to.

pages.title: Cultural spotlight
Reading quest — My first concert night
text: Tonight I went to my first concert in the USA with my friend Omar. I was very happy. At the door, a woman asked, “**Do you have your ticket?**” I showed my phone and she said, “Great. Go in.”

Inside, the room was big and **loud**. We asked, “**Where are our seats?**” Omar looked at his phone. “**Section B, row five**,” he said. We walked past many people and said, “Excuse me, sorry!” again and again.

The **band** started at eight. The **crowd** screamed and the **stage** lights were red and blue. One man next to me shouted, “**This show rocks!**” I sang the words with everyone. Soon I was **losing my voice**!

I remembered a school musical, “High School Musical.” It is a Disney film from 2006, and the students sing on a stage. Before the show, friends say, “**Break a leg!**” That means good luck. Tonight the band was the star.

After the last song, nobody went home. We all clapped and shouted, “**Encore!**” The band came back and played one more song. It was the **best night ever**. “**Enjoy the show!**” Omar said, and I did.
